resources.string: Monitors app launches and, in supported browsers, the address bar to block distracting apps and websites. Where you have chosen to block only part of an app, it also reads which section of that app is on screen (for example Reels rather than messages) so that only the section you chose is blocked. It also notices when you open Intention\'s own page in Settings, or the Accessibility settings for this service, and offers you a conversation with your coach before you switch it off or uninstall — it never blocks either, and never taps anything for you. It never controls or automates the apps you use. This helps you practice mindfulness via the Intention AI Coach.

Intention needs Accessibility permission (the AccessibilityService API) to block the apps and websites you choose and to let your coach talk you through opening them.

What it reads, while the service is on:
• The name of the app that is on screen, to see whether it is one you blocked.
• In supported browsers, the address in the address bar, to block the websites you chose.
• Only in an app where you blocked one part (for example Reels), the names of the on-screen sections, to tell which part is open. It never reads posts, messages, passwords or anything you type.
• Whether you have opened Intention's own page in Settings, so it can offer a word with your coach first. It never stops you leaving.

How it is used: all of this is checked on your phone against your own block list. None of it is stored or shared, with one exception: when you choose to talk to your coach, the name of the app or the address of the site you were opening is sent with your message to the AI service that answers it.

Intention never taps, types or controls other apps for you.

Do you agree to Intention using the Accessibility service this way?
Without Accessibility permission Intention can\'t block anything on this phone. You can agree at any time from this screen.
